nodes.label: Embedded SPA in Rust Binary
nodes.rationale: The web build output is compiled into the Rust binary via rust-embed so a release is a single executable serving API, static assets, and Swagger UI with no nginx or Node runtime in front of it.

nodes.label: Binary/Image Footprint Budget
nodes.rationale: "Functional, but not bloated" is treated as a product decision enforced by a CI-gated numeric budget (binary size, docker export rootfs size, startup RSS) rather than left as a per-PR argument.

nodes.label: Two-Tier Clippy Lint Policy
nodes.rationale: deny-level lints block cargo run for concurrency/safety mistakes that are wrong at any moment; warn-level lints (including all of pedantic) don't block local iteration but are enforced with -D warnings in CI, letting a contributor keep working while still catching issues at PR time.

nodes.label: Hand-written SQL Migrations Per Dialect
nodes.rationale: SeaORM's schema builder would collapse per-dialect migrations into one definition, but hand-written CREATE TABLE SQL is easier for a reviewer or operator to read than a chain of ColumnDef calls; the risk of dialects drifting apart is mitigated by a unit test comparing statement counts plus CI applying all three dialects for real.

nodes.label: Two-Crate Split (Compile-Time Layering Enforcement)
nodes.rationale: tessera-core deliberately has no dependency on axum, sea-orm, object_store or tokio, so business logic reaching for framework/IO code fails to compile rather than relying on review discipline; CI also checks the resolved dependency tree to catch transitive violations.
